content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: PD#INC-4821 — severity P1 — metric: lb.target_health_degraded (us-west2) — symptoms: TLS handshake failures + 5xx spike

pagerduty: Auto-acknowledged: maya (oncall)

maya (oncall): acked. I'm looking. starting with LB and edge certs.

ethan: any config pushes in us-west2 in last hour?

maya (oncall): nothing in deploy history. quick checks: edge logs show lots of `tls: handshake error` from our ALB layer. Examples:

```
2026-03-15T21:03:02Z edge-proxy us-west2 TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-03-15T21:03:14Z edge-proxy us-west2 TLS handshake error: no common signature algorithms
```

maya (oncall): doing an `aws elbv2 describe-target-health` now.

charlie-sre: can you paste the output? also run a quick curl to a failing host.

maya (oncall): curl gives: 

```bash
$ curl -v https://api.us-west2.redwood.example.com/health -I
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.us-west2.redwood.example.com/health
*   Trying 10.0.5.34...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.us-west2.redwood.example.com (10.0.5.34) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* SSL: certificate verify result: unable to get local issuer certificate (20), continuing anyway.
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* SSL: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
* Closing connection 0
```

maya (oncall): describe-target-health shows many targets in `initial` or `unhealthy` state, sample: 6/15 healthy in one TG.

leah: DNS? yesterday we lowered TTL to 300 while testing weight shift — could be partial propagation with bad endpoints still in DNS sets.

ethan: I see a recent change to the route table weights — PR merged ~40m ago that adjusted canary weights for us-west2.

charlie-sre: hypothesis: bad backend region config + low TTL → some clients hitting partially updated backends with mismatched certs or certs not loaded on new targets.

maya (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic away from us-west2 to eu-west1 90/10, 2) mark unhealthy targets OutOfService so we stop routing to them, 3) rotate cert on suspicious hosts if needed.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook check: For TLS spike with target health degraded — recommended immediate traffic shift + create incident in status page.

maya (oncall): applying weight shift now:

```bash
# infractl (internal)
infractl route update --service api --region us-west2 --weight 10 --region eu-west1 --weight 90 --reason "emergency failover: TLS+target health"
```

maya (oncall): applied. Confirming traffic telemetry...

ethan: telemetry shows egress to eu-west1 jumped, client error rate dropping in us-west2 but overall 5xx across platform still elevated (global ~2.4% -> baseline 0.2%).

maya (oncall): marking targets unhealthy in the TG to force replacement: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets` for hosts showing TLS errors.

charlie-sre: good — also adding an explicit hold on the weight-change PR until we fully validate.

leah: status page draft: "We are investigating increased TLS handshake errors and elevated error rates impacting API requests for some customers in US-West region. Traffic is being shifted to healthy regions. We'll post updates every 15 minutes." Approve?

maya (oncall): post it. include workaround: clients can retry or use eu-west endpoint while we remediate.

pagerduty: Escalation timer: 10m until PD escalation to secondary on-call.

robin: I'll take next shift to monitor the remediation and run cert checks across backends. @maya please handoff when you're ready.

maya (oncall): handoff prep: summarizing actions so far:
- Identified TLS handshake errors at edge + unhealthy LB targets in us-west2
- Shifted traffic to eu-west1 (90/10) via infractl
- Deregistered several unhealthy targets from TGs
- Posted initial status page update
- Monitoring error rate and client impact metrics

maya (oncall): handing off to @robin at 21:30Z. I will remain reachable for 15m overlap.

robin: ack handoff. next steps: run `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <host>` against a sample set, verify cert chain, and kick cert reload on any host returning chain errors. Also will work with infra to restore healthy targets and progressively shift traffic back.

ethan: note — DNS TTL of 300 means some clients still may hit cached us-west2 entries; expect partial recovery delay up to TTL.

leah: putting a follow-up item to add canary validation for weight-change PRs to avoid partial config states.

ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: create incident doc in the incidents folder and link to this thread.

maya (oncall): creating incident doc now. tagging product and support for customer comms.

charlie-sre: great work. final check: estimated customer impact: ~8% of hosted API requests in us-west2 experienced timeouts/5xx between 21:00-21:20Z; global customer-facing errors peaked at ~2.4% and are trending down after traffic shift.

robin: thanks, taking over monitoring. will update thread on final traffic restore plan and postmortem notes.
